english: Let $B$ and $C$ be $2\times2$ real orthogonal matrices, each with determinant $1$, whose first columns are $\begin{pmatrix}\frac45\\[2pt]\frac35\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{12}{13}\\[2pt]\frac{5}{13}\end{pmatrix}$, respectively. If $B^{T}C=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\r&s\end{pmatrix}$, where $B^{T}$ is the transpose of $B$, then the value of $65(p+q)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $B$ तथा $C$, $2\times2$ वास्तविक लांबिक (orthogonal) आव्यूह हैं, प्रत्येक का सारणिक $1$ है, तथा इनके प्रथम स्तम्भ क्रमशः $\begin{pmatrix}\frac45\\[2pt]\frac35\end{pmatrix}$ तथा $\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{12}{13}\\[2pt]\frac{5}{13}\end{pmatrix}$ हैं। यदि $B^{T}C=\begin{pmatrix}p&q\\r&s\end{pmatrix}$ है, जहाँ $B^{T}$, $B$ का परिवर्त है, तो $65(p+q)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Orthogonal with determinant $1$ and first column $\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta\\\sin\theta\end{pmatrix}$: second column is a unit vector perpendicular to it with $\det=1$, i.e. $\begin{pmatrix}-\sin\theta\\\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$; so the matrix is $R_\theta$
solution_full: A real $2\times2$ matrix is orthogonal exactly when its columns are perpendicular unit vectors.

If the first column is $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)^{T}$, the second column is a unit vector perpendicular to it, so it is $\pm(-\sin\theta,\cos\theta)^{T}$; the determinant condition $\det=1$ selects the $+$ sign. So the matrix is $R_\theta=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$.
Thus $B=R_\alpha$ with $\cos\alpha=\frac45$, $\sin\alpha=\frac35$, and $C=R_\beta$ with $\cos\beta=-\frac{12}{13}$, $\sin\beta=\frac{5}{13}$ (both first columns are unit vectors).
originality_note: New: two orthogonal matrices are known only by their first columns and determinant; the product B^T C is read as a rotation through beta - alpha, so the entries come from compound angles with Pythagorean triples 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 (way 5). Closest known: R(alpha) R(beta) = R(alpha + beta) for rotation matrices. Different because: the second columns must be reconstructed from orthogonality and the sign of the determinant, and the transpose turns the sum into a difference.

concept_use.Orthogonal matrices: Orthogonality with det 1 fixes the second columns (B and C are rotation matrices) and gives B^T = B^{-1} = R_{-alpha}.
concept_use.Compound angles: sin(A+/-B), cos(A+/-B),: B^T C = R_{beta - alpha}, with cos(beta - alpha) = -33/65 and sin(beta - alpha) = 56/65 from the compound-angle formulas.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy builds B and C, confirms BB^T = CC^T = I and det = 1, and gives B^T C = [[-33/65, -56/65],[56/65, -33/65]], so 65(p + q) = -89 (a negative integer as planned). Changed: added 'each with determinant 1', without which the second columns are not unique.
key_step: Recognising B and C as rotation matrices from orthogonality and det = 1, then B^T C = R_{beta - alpha}.
justification: Routine chain: reconstruct the rotation matrices, use B^T = B^{-1}, apply compound angles. The orthogonality idea is used directly, unlike the hidden use in 2026-P1-Q15 (L4); at the routine level of 2021-P1-Q11 (L2).
